items.title: NOON
items.note: The Quietus made this their album of the week. It pairs the Lancashire composer with the Room40 boss, and the review says the two find "a still point in the midst of the storm of contemporary history".
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (via The Quietus)

items.title: 711Falx
items.note: A debut album and the first release on Fovea Specs. Bandcamp Daily heard dubby chord stabs and crinkly pads with a sneaky sense of motion, and the label notes nods to 2-step and footwork along the way.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (via Bandcamp Daily)

items.artist: Sylvia Meyer & Lila Tirando a Violeta
items.title: Doble Ceniza
items.note: A five-track EP where two Uruguayan artists from different generations meet. Sylvia Meyer's old piano and voice demos are reshaped with field recordings and fragments, and Bandcamp Daily called it a blissful, mostly beatless listen.

items.title: Khudgarzi
items.note: Her first full album, on Erased Tapes, sung mostly in Urdu over Hindustani, Carnatic, Turkish and Arabic instruments. Bandcamp Daily says it filters traditional currents into futuristic electronic landscapes, like her mentor Arooj Aftab with a bit more bite.

items.title: MO LÉAN (Expanded)
items.note: An expanded international edition, via Domino, of her 2024 album, so not strictly new, but worth it. She reworks the Irish funeral lament with electronics, and Bandcamp Daily points to the trip-hop of "Cití" and the ambient-to-dub drift of "Oh Lovely Appearance of Death".

items.title: All Ages
items.note: A new album for Warp. The Quietus interviewed him about the skateboarding and hardcore scenes that shaped him as a teenager, and the rebellion against himself that went into making it.

items.title: East Side Love Story
items.note: A debut made over six years in East LA and co-produced with Chris McClenney, drawing on Chicano soul, Motown and G-funk. Bandcamp Daily called it one of the year's most swoon-worthy debuts.

items.title: Diana
items.note: A guitar quartet record on ECM. Jazz Views called it a marvellous set of original compositions that pull at the ears and the heart.

items.title: Riders of the Setting Sun
items.note: The band leave their black metal past behind for gothic Americana built on acoustic guitar, slide and memorable melodies. David Eugene Edwards and Jay Munly guest, according to Bandcamp Daily's album of the day write-up.

items.title: On Course But No-One There To Salute You
items.note: Partly recorded at 4AD's studios. I could only read The Quietus feed summary, which calls it "less sunburst and snowblind than wind-battered and rain-sodden", so give it a listen before you buy.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (via The Quietus)
